# Introduction

The following document is the specification of the REST API for Process Management. It includes the model definition as well as all available operations. Possible actions are creating, updating, and retrieving Process, ProcessSpecification, Task and TaskSpecification.

The TMF701 Process Management API allows management of business process definition and execution. It manages Process, ProcessSpecification, Task and TaskSpecification resources:

- A ProcessSpecification is a business process specification described in a BPMN engine or hard coded. It describes relationship with other entity specification but also party involved in this specification design. A ProcessSpecification will define an orchestration of TaskSpecification. A TaskSpecification could be re-used by several ProcessSpecification.
- A Process represents an instance of a pre-designed ProcessSpecification. It defines a start point, an orchestration of task (that could be dynamically instantiated) and end point(s). Entities involved in the process completion could be related to the process.
- A TaskSpecification is a business process task specification – in other words, a “work” description to be done within a ProcessSpecification.
- A Task is an instantiation of a TaskSpecification. It could be completed automatically (send an email, execute a business rule, wait for an event triggered by an external system) or requiring manual action (a form to be completed).

TMF701 Process Management API performs the following operations on ProcessSpecification resource:

- Retrieval of a ProcessSpecification or a collection of ProcessSpecification(s) depending on filter criteria
- Creation of a ProcessSpecification
- Partial update a ProcessSpecification
- Deletion of ProcessSpecification
- Notification of events on ProcessSpecification

    - ProcessSpecification creation
    - ProcessSpecification status change
    - ProcessSpecification deletion
    - ProcessSpecification attribute value change

![](data:image/png;base64,)

…on TaskSpecification resource:

- Retrieval of a TaskSpecification or a collection of TaskSpecification(s) depending on filter criteria
- Creation of TaskSpecification
- Partial update of a TaskSpecification
- Deletion of TaskSpecification
- Notification of events on TaskSpecification

    - TaskSpecification creation
    - TaskSpecification status change
    - TaskSpecification deletion
    - TaskSpecification attribute value change

… on Process resource:

- Retrieval of a Process or a collection of Process(s) depending on filter criteria
- Creation of a Process
- Deletion of Process(for administration purposes)
- Notification of events on Process

    - Process creation
    - Process status change
    - Process deletion
    - Process attribute value change

And on Task resource:

- Retrieval of a Task or a collection of Task(s) depending on filter criteria
- Creation of a Task
- Partial update of a Task
- Deletion of a Task
- Notification of events on Task

    - Task creation
    - Task status change
    - Task deletion

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Task information required
- Task attribute value change

The following assumptions were considered in the development of this document: The process management API should rely on a BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) tool but nothing prevents if from having a hard-coded component.

# Sample Use Cases

Reader will find example of use cases using Process API in "How to use ODA – Using Open APIs to realize Use Cases IG1228" TMF document.

To illustrate JSON we will use the following example of a definition of a ProcessSpecification featuring 5 TaskSpecification (tfs99, tfs0, tfs1, tfs2 and tfs3). For the Process & task examples we use instances of theses specifications.

## Example of an order capture ProcessSpecification

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Example of an order capture Process Instance

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

For this use case, we will use an orderCapture business process that will manage a ‘shoppingCart’ initialization and completion as a process example. The process is very simple:

- The order Capture process is launched with contextual information about the interaction, we assume that the customer identification is already done and is not part of this process.
- A productOffering may be passed in the first request. If not the first task will be to ask for one from the customer. For simplification purposes, we assume it to be a "main offer".
- Then, a check on the commercial eligibility should be done.
- Once commercial eligibility confirmed, a shoppingCart is intialized.
- After shopping cart configuration and user acknowledgement, a task is performed to check cart completion, if it’s successful an orderCompletion Process is launched.

This example leverage existing TMF API as productCatalog, productOfferingQualification, shoppingCart, productOrder, etc… These APIs use will not be illustrated in this document (done within task execution).

**These examples are only for illustration purposes, and they must not be considered as** **process guideline.**

## Process and Task Lifecycle

The proposed lifecycle has been inspired from the BPMN standard (Business Process Model and Notation), it outlines the various states a task or a process can transition through, including initiation, execution, possible interruption, and conclusion, with specific conditions guiding each transition.

| **State** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| Ready | The process or task is in a Ready state when it’s ready to startbut hasn’t been initiated because necessary inputs are not yetprovided. |
| Planned | The process or task is in a Planned state when it’s beenscheduled for later, once the start time is reached it coulddirectly start or pass to Ready state if inputs are not yetprovided. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **State** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| Active | The process or task is initiated and is currently beingexecuted. It is in progress and can transition to various otherstates based on different conditions. |
| Completed | The process or task has been successfully completed and allrequired actions have been fulfilled. |
| Withdrawn | The process or task is withdrawn by the user or system beforecompletion. This could be due to a change in requirements orother external factors. It may be required to perform a rollbackon the executed actions. |
| Terminated | The process or task has been forcibly stopped before it couldbe completed, often due to critical issues, errors, or conditionsthat make it impossible or unsafe to continue. |
| Failed | The process or task has failed to complete due to anunrecoverable error or condition. |
| Suspended | A temporary pause in process or task execution whereactivities are halted but can be resumed later. |

# Illustration Use Case

This section aims to demonstrate the usage of the TMF701 Process Management API through a generic example. A simplified BPMN is utilized for illustration purposes, alongside JSON request and response messages. These messages showcase the use of TMF701 resources, specifically process and task .

Please note that the goal of this section is not to provide a fully compliant ODA UC. For a detailed description of fully compliant UCs, please refer to the TMF official document IG1228. This example is intended for illustrative purposes only.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Order Capture Use case

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Several patterns are illustrated:

- **Synchronous interaction**: After a new party interaction on a Front End (FE), this later invokes the Back End (BE) to request what are the next possible actions (what is/are the action(s) available for this party in the context of this interaction). This flow is a synchronous request/response
- **Synchronous interaction featuring Process delegation**: Once the choice is confirmed by the user through the FE, the running process has to trigger another process which will be responsible to execute the requested choice. the BE has to provide all information to the FE seamlessly. This flow is a synchronous request/response.
- **Asynchronous Event-based interaction**: Later, during the configuration of the shopping cart, the running process has to manage a task. This task is asynchronous. An acknowledgement is sent to the FE. Once the task completed, the process triggers an event. the FE is identified as listener and get a notification about next task to be performed.

**Illustration 1 – Synchronous interaction**

**BPMN View**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Flows description (flow 1 and 2)**:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

A party initiates a session on the web. The frontend triggers a message to the backend to launch a welcome process. This process is launched and the BE sends directly in the response to the frontend the next task to be performed describing the list of actions available to the user ‘to be proposed’ to the party for this interaction context (depending on the channel, the requesting app, if the party is identified, etc…).

The processSpecification indicates the type of the process to be created. In order to transfer interaction context, the requester could use 3 substructures:

- Channel: the channel where the interaction is.
- relatedParty: it could be used to describe any individual or organization involved in this interaction (not present in this example), for example:

    - the customer if he/she is identified
    - the sales organization for a contact in retail
    - etc…

- relatedEntity: a generic structure to describe any other entity related to this interaction.

For this initialization, the FE is not ‘guided’ by a previous interaction and has to trigger a request to create a “Welcome process” (1 POST Process Welcome Request).

**1 POST Process Welcome Request**

```
POST  /process
{
  "channel": [
    {
      "id": "12",
      "name": "OnlineCRMapp",
      "href":" "https://www.mycsp.com/tmfapis/channel/12",
      "@type":"ChannelRef",
      "@referredType":"Channel"
    }  ],
  "relatedParty": [    {
      "role": "Customer",
      "@type": "RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef",
      "partyOrPartyRole": {        "id": "456-f69",

This message triggers the creation of a new process instance (here the process 45kl-98io is created). The first task “Provide user choices” will have to trigger the following actions:

- Create a PartyInteraction to track this interaction with an id – We’ll trigger the PartyInteraction management process, asking the creation of new partyInteraction and getting partyInteraction.id in response
- Check and identify the list of processes available and allowed for this interaction context (Browse catalog, order capture, etc…) – the list of processes depends on a pre- defined rules and data provided as an input
- Provide response to the FE with following information:

    - Id of the process created
    - Id of the PartyInteraction created instance
    - List of available processes to display as a choices for the user
    - Description of the ‘task’ to update in order to provide the answer.

The answer will be something like the flow 2 (2 POST Process Welcome Response).

### Illustration 2 – Synchronous Process Transfer

### BPMN View

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Flows description (flow 3, 4, 5 and 6)**:

The user on the front picks one choice, let’s assume that he/she wants to order something. The Front End triggers the PATCH task of the instance fg66-55aa to indicate the user choice. In this example this choice will not be managed by the running welcome process

![](data:image/png;base64,)

but another process flow needs to be triggered (in charge of order capture). The Welcome process triggers the Order Capture process. This one is initialized and its technical details are provided in the response (id, href, status, …). Welcome process gets this information and provides it to the Front End.

Based on the id and href, the Front End will be able to consult the order capture process and to get details about running tasks and how to proceed to continue the ordering.

**3 PATCH task fg66-55aa Request**

```
PATCH process/45kl-98io/task/fg66-55aa{
  "taskCharacteristic": [    {
        "modality":"input",
        "@type":"FlowCharacteristic",
        "characteristic":{
          "name": "User selected choice",
          "valueType": "string",
          "value":  "OrderCapture",
          "@type": "StringCharacteristic"        }
    }  ],
  "@type": "Task"}
```

The main information here is the characteristic value, which will define the process wished by the user. In our example this choice will trigger a set of operations, described implicitly & explicitly in the previous bpmn diagram:

- Check process choice is valid
- Manage the choice – here a new process instance must be triggered to manage the order capture
- Order capture process is triggered and first tasks are ready to start: request main offer to confirm eligibility, start the configuration, and create a shoppingCart resource
- Once the order capture process is launched, the initial welcome process has to provide the information to the FE for the next interaction.
- Terminate Welcome process The order capture process launch is a backend to backend delegation. The welcome process will trigger the following message 4 POST process Order Capture.

### Illustration 3 – Asynchronous Event-based interaction

### BPMN View

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Once the FE helped the user to pick a main offer (it will use GET productOffering from the productCatalog API to retrieve catalog information and display them to the user), it will use the URL of the running task “Confirm selected main offer” provided by the 'order capture' process to update it with the selected offer. Once the task got this information, eligibility check could be performed and if fine the task could send an acknowledgment to the FE.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The offer choice allows moving to the next task ‘Get configured shoppingCart’. In our illustration this task creation triggers an event (taskInformationRequiredEvent =⇒ ConfiguredCartRequired). This event is sent to an Event management component. This component get the event, retrieve event information and based on preconfigured rules, it will make the event available to the listener(s). Here we assumed the FE is already a presubscribed listener to this event type (taskInformationRequiredEvent).

The FE will recieve a notification including the related event information. With this information it will know about the next action to perform and with same pattern as the previous exchange.

The TMF688 event API (draft API targeted for v5) is used first to trigger from the OC process the (ConfiguredCartRequired) event.

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a BillingAccount and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 TMF630.

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of BillingAccount where other could be instances of SettlementAccount. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as BillingAccountRef or SettlementAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**CharacteristicSpecification sub-resource fields**

This class defines a characteristic specification.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| characteristicValueSpecification | A CharacteristicValueSpecification \[0..\*\]. A CharacteristicValueSpecification object is used to define a set ofattributes, each of which can be assigned to acorresponding set of attributes in a CharacteristicSpecification object. The values of the attributes in theCharacteristicValueSpecification object describe thevalues of the attributes that a correspondingCharacteristic object can take on.CharacteristicValueSpecification can be instantiated as\* BooleanArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* BooleanCharacteristicValueSpecification\* FloatArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* FloatCharacteristicValueSpecification\* IntegerArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* IntegerCharacteristicValueSpecification\* MapArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* MapCharacteristicValueSpecification\* NumberArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* NumberCharacteristicValueSpecification\* ObjectArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* ObjectCharacteristicValueSpecification\* StringArrayCharacteristicValueSpecification\* StringCharacteristicValueSpecification |
| --- | --- |
| charSpecRelationship | A CharacteristicSpecificationRelationship \[0..\*\]. Anaggregation, migration, substitution, dependency orexclusivity relationship between/among SpecificationCharacteristics. |
| configurable | A Boolean. If true, the Boolean indicates that the targetCharacteristic is configurable. |
| description | A String. A narrative that explains the CharacteristicSpecification. |
| extensible | A Boolean. An indicator that specifies that the values forthe characteristic can be extended by adding new valueswhen instantiating a characteristic for a resource. |
| id | A String. Unique ID for the characteristic. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| isUnique | A Boolean. Specifies if the value of this characteristic isunique across all entities instantiated from thespecification that uses this characteristic. For example,consider a ProductSpecification for a set-top box, with aCharacteristicSpecification cardID. Each set-top box musthave a different value for cardID, so this isUnique attributewould be set to true for the characteristic. |
| --- | --- |
| maxCardinality | An Integer. The maximum number of instances aCharacteristicValue can take on. For example, zero to fivephone numbers in a group calling plan, where five is thevalue for the maxCardinality. |
| minCardinality | An Integer. The minimum number of instances aCharacteristicValue can take on. For example, zero to fivephone numbers in a group calling plan, where zero is thevalue for the minCardinality. |
| name | A String \[1\]. A word, term, or phrase by which thischaracteristic specification is known and distinguishedfrom other characteristic specifications. |
| regex | A String. A rule or principle represented in regularexpression used to derive the value of a characteristicvalue. |
| validFor | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |
| valueType | A String \[1\]. A kind of value that the characteristic can takeon, such as numeric, text and so forth. |

| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that definesadditional attributes and relationships. |

# Field descriptions

# Process fields

| channel | A ChannelRef. The channel to which the resourcereference to. e.g. channel for selling product offerings,channel for opening a trouble ticket etc.. |
| --- | --- |
| completionDate | A DateTime. Effective completion date for this process. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Is the date when the process was created(timestamp). |
| description | A String. Description of the process. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| externalIdentifier | An ExternalIdentifier. An identification of an entity that isowned by or originates in a software system differentfrom the current system, for example a ProductOrderhanded off from a commerce platform into an orderhandling system. The structure identifies the system itself,the nature of the entity within the system (e.g. classname) and the unique ID of the entity within the system. Itis anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for asingle entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiplesystems on the way to the current system. In this casethe consumer is expected to sequence the IDs in thearray in reverse order of provenance, i.e. most recentsystem first in the list. |
| --- | --- |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| name | A String. The name of the process. |
| processCharacteristic | A FlowCharacteristic \[0..\*\]. A list of characteristic(s)associated to this process, capturing contextualinformation such as parameters, conditions, orconfiguration values that may influence its execution,such us priority, retryLimit, or qualityRate. |
| processRelationship | A ProcessRelationship \[0..\*\]. A list of links connecting thecurrent process to other process instances, withrelationshipType specifying the nature of eachrelationship (e.g., triggers/triggeredBy, delegates/delegatedBy, dependsOn/requiredBy). |
| processSpecification | A ProcessSpecificationRef \[1\]. A reference to a processspecification defined on design time. |
| relatedEntity | A RelatedEntity \[0..\*\]. A list of related entity(ies) to thisprocess. |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef \[0..\*\]. A list of relatedparty(ies) to this process. |
| requestedCompletionDate | A DateTime. Requested completion date for this process. |
| requestedStartDate | A DateTime. Requested start date for this process. |
| startDate | A DateTime. Effective start date for this process. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| state | A FlowStateType. Possible values for the state of the Flow.ENUMERATED with values:\* ready\* planned\* active\* withdrawn\* terminated\* failed\* completed\* other |
| --- | --- |
| task | A TaskRefOrValue \[0..\*\]. A list of taskRef or task valuesrelated to this process. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that definesadditional attributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String \[1\]. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

**ChannelRef sub-resource fields**

The channel to which the resource reference to. e.g. channel for selling product offerings, channel for opening a trouble ticket etc..

See \[ChannelRef\] for details.

**ExternalIdentifier sub-resource fields**

An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different from the current system, for example a ProductOrder handed off from a commerce platform into an order handling system. The structure identifies the system itself, the nature of the entity within the system (e.g. class name) and the unique ID of the entity within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this case the consumer is expected to sequence the IDs in the array in reverse order of provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.

| externalIdentifierType | A String. Type of the identification, typically would be thetype of the entity within the external system. |
| --- | --- |
| id | A String \[1\]. Identification of the entity within the externalsystem. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| owner | A String. Name of the external system that owns theentity. |
| --- | --- |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that definesadditional attributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String \[1\]. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

**FlowCharacteristic sub-resource fields**

Describes a given characteristic of a flow through a name/value pair. This is an abstract base class, the actual value is in one of the strongly-typed subclasses : String Characteristic, ObjectCharacteristic, FloatCharacteristic, BooleanCharacteristic, Number Characteristic, IntegerCharacteristic, StringArrayCharacteristic, ObjectArrayCharacteristic, BooleanArrayCharacteristic, NumberArrayCharacteristic, IntegerArrayCharacteristic...

| characteristic | A Characteristic \[1\]. Describes a given characteristic of anobject or entity through a name/value pair. ### TaskSpecification resource

TaskSpecification is a class that allow to describe a task design. A task design defines the tasks that can potentially be instantiated within a process that is instantiated from this process specification.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| attachment | An AttachmentRefOrValue \[0..\*\]. Attachments that are ofrelevance to this TaskSpecification, such as picture,document, media. This could be for example a how-to or afaq to explain this TaskSpecification. |
| --- | --- |
| channel | A ChannelRef \[0..\*\]. A list of channels where Tasksinstantiated from this TaskSpecification could beexecuted. |
| description | A String. Description of the TaskSpecification. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| lastUpdate | A DateTime. Date and time of the last update of the TaskSpecification. |
| lifecycleStatus | A String. Used to indicate the current lifecycle status ofthis TaskSpecification, for example: onDesign, active,deprecated. |
| name | A String \[1\]. Name given to the TaskSpecification. |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef \[0..\*\]. Parties whomanage or otherwise have an interest in this TaskSpecification. |
| relatedProcessSpecification | A RelatedProcessSpecification \[0..\*\]. A related ProcessSpecification (for example when the TaskSpecificationcompletion requires another ProcessSpecification to betriggered & completed). |
| taskSpecificationCharacteristic | A FlowCharacteristicSpecification \[0..\*\]. List ofcharacteristics that the TaskSpecification can take. |
| taskSpecificationPolicy | A PolicyRef \[0..\*\]. A list of policies related to this taskSpecification. |
| taskSpecificationRelationship | A TaskSpecificationRelationship \[0..\*\]. A list of tasksrelated to this task, representing dependencies,sequencing, or logical associations. |
| taskType | A String. The type of the task, the BPMN standarddistinguish different types of tasks like sendTask, receiveTask, userTask, manualTask, scriptTask, businessRuleTask. |
| validFor | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |

## Notification Resource Models

17 notifications are defined for this API.

Notifications related to ProcessSpecification:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

Notifications related to Process:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

Notifications related to Task:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- Information Required Event
- State Change Event

Notifications related to TaskSpecification:

- Create Event
- Delete Event

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

# API OPERATIONS

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| **Operation on Entities** | **Uniform API Operation** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrievea representation of aresource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to createa new resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used topartially update a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on anEntity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used toexecute Task Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Updates partially a processSpecification

### PATCH /processSpecification/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a ProcessSpecification entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| attachment |  |
| channel |  |
| description |  |
| lastUpdate |  |
| lifecycleStatus |  |
| name |  |
| processSpecificationCharacteristic |  |
| processSpecificationPolicy |  |
| processSpecificationRelationship |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| taskSpecification |  |
| validFor |  |
| version |  |

```

```
204
```

### Updates partially a process `PATCH /process/{id}?fields=…`

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of a Process entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| processSpecification |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| channel |  |
| completionDate |  |
| description |  |
| externalIdentifier |  |
| name |  |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| processCharacteristic |  |
| processRelationship |  |
| relatedEntity |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| requestedCompletionDate |  |
| requestedStartDate |  |
| startDate |  |
| state |  |
| task |  |

### Deletes a process

```
DELETE /process/{id}?{filtering}
```

**Description**

This operation deletes a Process entity.

**Usage samples**

Here’s an example of a request for delete a specific process

**Request**

```
DELETE /process/4fd-ty56-gg55Content-Type: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

### Updates partially a task

### PATCH /task/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a Task entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH

![](data:image/png;base64,)

operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| completionDate |  |
| startDate |  |
| taskSpecification |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| channel |  |
| description |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| isMandatory |  |
| name |  |
| parentProcess |  |
| priority |  |
| relatedEntity |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| relatedProcess |  |
| state |  |
| taskCharacteristic |  |
| taskRelationship |  |
| taskType |  |

### Updates partially a taskSpecification

### PATCH /taskSpecification/{id}?fields=…

### Description

This operation allows partial updates of a TaskSpecification entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| lifecycleStatus |  |

| validFor |  |
| version |  |

# API NOTIFICATIONS

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
